mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS rise, or the S&P 500 returns to its pre-move trend within 5 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting stronger consumer demand.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (current value + 50,000) in the following month
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) in any 60-day window following the job gain threshold, or the effect persists only in contractionary periods.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) show double-digit month-over-month growth in the next two months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, signaling robust supply-demand balance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > (current + 10%) AND HOUST > (current + 10%) in the next two months
failure_condition: No significant positive return (Rank IC < 0.05) during the defined growth window, or either proxy fails to meet the growth threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 5 points or more over the next month predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return, as it suggests weakening manufacturing capacity and tighter balance sheets.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline, or the effect is absent in non-crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling UNRATE (unemployment) below 4%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to increased investor confidence and reduced risk aversion.
failure_condition: No significant positive return (p > 0.05) in any 20-day window following the UNRATE threshold, or the effect reverses in subsequent months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp spike in RSAFS (retail sales) of over 10% in the next month, accompanied by a decline in UNRATE below 5%, predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as retail spending accelerates and uncertainty falls.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > (current * 1.10) AND UNRATE < 5.0 in the following month
regime_hint: rebound in retail activity with easing labor market
failure_condition: No significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) during the interaction window, or either proxy fails to meet the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in the next two months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to anticipated future inflation pressures eroding equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > (current * 1.005) over the next two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the CPI rise, or the effect is absent in non-inflationary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (goods orders) of 15% followed by a rise in HOUST (production) above current levels within the same month predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as the market anticipates demand recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < (current * 0.85) AND HOUST > current in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive return (Rank IC < 0.05) during the defined pattern, or the order decline persists beyond the month.
